why: `e as T` checks nothing at run time (the emit drops it), and neither does an any or unknown value filling a typed slot. The proof lane read such a value as an uninterpreted conversion into T and then read T's operations exactly, so `x as number` on a string | number, `x as string` on unknown, `JSON.parse(s) as { a: number }` and an any parameter in a number local were each proved equal to a candidate adding 0 or "" ("a" + 0 is "a0"). Now the value is read with its real type (common.mjs assertionHeld): the opaque Any for an any or unknown source or a source mixing types, the source's own type for one primitive family. `v + 0` is then an uninterpreted operation on Any and differs from `v`: the four are not proved, lane B witnesses each. widen (to a supertype), rank (a literal into its union), bump (a number asserted to a literal union, read as the number) and twice (the same operation on an opaque value on both sides) are proved beside plain. optAny holds an any value in a string | undefined local: it is read opaque in its definedness and its payload, so `s + ""` differs from `s` (not proved, lane B WITNESS); optChecked fills the same slot through a typeof test and is proved. Lane B: optChecked is a WITNESS on -0 (an unknown parameter meets the special numbers, design/gen-walk.md 2026-10-30): the parent returns -0 and the candidate's n + 0 returns +0, so JavaScript tells them apart; lane A's proof is over the reals (real-only), which leave -0 out. The four slots a held value could not reach (design/type-assertions.md, 2026-10-30): a field of a literal (fieldHeld proved: the field is Any in the literal's own datatype, and the record reaches the declared result type by one uninterpreted conversion; fieldBumped not proved), a same-file callee's parameter (paramHeld: the callee is read once more with that parameter at Any; paramKept not proved), a call of a unit whose result is held (resultHeld: the call reads the unit once more, returning Any; resultBumped not proved), a compound write (compoundHeld: `t += v` reads the target's real type, Any; compoundBumped not proved). The six rows of the last three slots return a template string: a number result read from Any may be the input itself, so the identity guard withholds it (as anyAs). paramHeld, resultHeld and compoundHeld are real-only, as twice: the real lemma proves, the doubles reading does not encode Any. Each must-not-prove row is witnessed by lane B on the emitted JavaScript, where the assertion is gone and a string flows on ("a" + 0 is "a0").
